Hi Maria —

As we discussed in last week's renewal call, Acme's H2 roadmap needs a predictable GPU pool with a slightly higher baseline and faster scale-up for short marketing bursts. Attached is a clean amendment (redwood-dedicated-amendment-v2.pdf) plus the estimate workbook that maps throughput to GPU counts (acme-capacity-estimate-uptick.xlsx).

Key proposal (summary):
- Add 40 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs to your Dedicated pool for the 12-month renewal term (committed capacity).
- Autoscale profile: min_replicas=6, max_replicas=46; warm buffer pool=6 GPUs (pre-warmed instances kept idle for instant scale); target scale-up lag goal=90s for first incremental replica, 240s to reach peak.
- Throughput guarantee: 95th percentile latency for 2k-token requests <= 350ms on balanced quantization profile when using the reserved pool.
- Optional: temporary burst allowance (+20% capacity) billed as overage at reduced burst rate for campaign windows.

Ben, can you confirm the cost delta for the committed uplift vs. a pay-as-you-go buffer and outline the recommended billing approach (commit + burst vs. lower commit + larger burst)? Maria, if this looks directionally correct, we'll move legal & procurement to the amendment and route DocuSign.

Thanks —

Nice summary, Tessa. A few clarifications and an option set for Acme:

(Quoted) On Wed, 11 Apr 2028 at 09:22 AM Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acmecorp.com> wrote:
> 1) That scale-up lag goal (90s -> 240s) — can you clarify whether that assumes the warm buffer is charged as committed capacity or is it billed as a warm-pool premium?
> 2) For the throughput guarantee, what's the remediation if the 95th percentile target is missed (credits, rollback, or priority routing)?
> 3) Are any changes needed on our side for networking (VPC peering, firewall rules) to support the warm buffer or is this transparent?

Answers / options:
- Warm buffer billing: we can offer the warm buffer in two ways: (A) included as part of the committed 40 GPUs (i.e., you pay the committed rate and we earmark N GPUs to stay pre-initialized), or (B) as a separate warm-pool premium (10% surcharge on top of hourly) billed only while buffer is maintained. Option A is simpler for forecasting; Option B reduces your committed spend but adds operational variance.

- Remediation for SLO misses: standard is a service credit ladder tied to downtime / sustained latency breaches. For throughput SLOs we propose: 5% credit for a single-day breach, 15% credit for a multi-day sustained breach, plus an ops review and optional free burst allowance during remediation windows. We can also include a runbook for priority routing to alternate pools in case of infra incidents.

- Networking: no additional VPC peering changes required for the warm buffer itself — warm instances live in your existing Dedicated pool and use the same networking. If Acme elects cross-region failover we will need peering/egress adjustments.

Cost scenarios (monthly delta vs current commitment):
1) Conservative: commit +6 warm buffer included — +$28k/mo — lowest overage exposure.
2) Balanced (recommended): commit +40 GPUs, warm buffer charged as premium during campaign windows — +$72k/mo base, bursts billed at reduced overage rate.
3) Aggressive: lower commit (20 GPUs) + larger burst window (pay-as-you-go up to +60 GPUs) — +$40k/mo base but higher burst variability.

I'll attach a quick cost sheet in the workbook (tab: pricing-options). Laura, can you prepare an amendment draft with the balanced option (2) language and the SLO credit ladder?

-Ben
Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
